extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and patent practitioners (patent owners and third-party requesters) involved in ex parte and inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for handling requests, petitions, patent owner statements, and proposed amendments in ex parte and inter partes reexamination proceedings before the USPTO, including formatting, timing, service, and reassignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition under 37 CFR 1.515(c) — timing and finality
rubrics_metrics.description: The requester may seek review by a petition to the Director under § 1.181 within one month of the mailing date of the examiner’s determination refusing ex parte reexamination; any such petition must comply with § 1.181(b). If no petition is timely filed or if the decision on petition affirms that no substantial new question of patentability has been raised, the determination shall be final and nonappealable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CRU allows time for the petition; a decision on a petition under 37 CFR 1.515(c) is final and not appealable. 37 CFR 1.515(c) applies only to challenging bases for denial of reexamination, not to challenging bases for granting reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRU Director review of petitions — de novo and possible grant effects
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition seeking review of the examiner’s determination refusing reexamination is filed, it is forwarded to the Office of the CRU Director for decision. The CRU Director’s review will be de novo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petition is granted, the decision should include a sentence setting a 2-month period for filing a statement under 37 CFR 1.530; the reexamination file will then be returned to the CRU Supervisory Patent Reexamination Specialist for consideration of reassignment to another examiner. Reassignment will be the general rule; exceptions only in exceptional circumstances (e.g., no other examiner available with requisite technology knowledge).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial refund after concluded denial or unsuccessful petition
rubrics_metrics.description: After the time for petition has expired without a petition filed, or a petition has been filed and the decision thereon affirms the denial of the request, a partial refund of the filing fee for requesting reexamination will be made to the requester (35 U.S.C. 303(c) and 37 CFR 1.26(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the financial processing consequence when denial becomes final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner’s statement timing (37 CFR 1.530(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The order for ex parte reexamination will set a period of not less than two months from the date of the order within which the patent owner may file a statement on the new question of patentability, including any proposed amendments the patent owner wishes to make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If necessary, an extension beyond the 2 months may be requested under 37 CFR 1.550(c); such extension granted only in extraordinary situations (e.g., death or incapacitation of representative or owner).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner’s statement content requirement (37 CFR 1.530(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any statement filed by the patent owner shall clearly point out why the subject matter as claimed is not anticipated or rendered obvious by the prior art patents or printed publications, either alone or in any reasonable combinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the reexamination request was filed by a third party requester, any statement filed by the patent owner must be served upon the requester in accordance with § 1.248. Lack of proof of service can cause the statement to be considered inappropriate and may be denied consideration (see MPEP § 2267).

rubrics_metrics.name: Premature patent owner statements are disregarded
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in § 1.510(e), no statement or other response by the patent owner in an ex parte reexamination proceeding shall be filed prior to the determinations made in accordance with § 1.515 or § 1.520. If a premature statement or other response is filed by the patent owner, it will not be acknowledged or considered and will be returned or discarded (at the Office’s option).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Premature statements may be expunged if inadvertently entered into the record (Patlex Corp. v. Mossinghoff cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and proof of service requirement for patent owner statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any statement filed by the patent owner in response to a reexamination order must be served on the requester (unless the request was filed by the patent owner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proof of service is omitted, CRU should contact the patent owner for a supplemental paper indicating manner and date of service; if patent owner cannot be contacted, CRU will contact the requester to verify service. If the 2‑month period under 37 CFR 1.530 has expired and requester has not been served, the patent owner’s statement is considered inappropriate and may be denied consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester's reply timing (37 CFR 1.535) — service-date trigger
rubrics_metrics.description: The period for response by requester for a reply under 37 CFR 1.535 is 2 months from the owner’s service date and not 2 months from the date the patent owner’s statement was received in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that the clock for requester’s reply is measured from service on requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of patent owner’s statement (Waiver Program)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the patent owner has determined that a statement under 37 CFR 1.530 will not be filed, the patent owner may expedite the reexamination proceeding by filing a paper indicating that the patent owner waives the filing of a statement under 37 CFR 1.530 and serving the waiver on the requester, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRU will contact the patent owner by telephone to request the optional waiver after a reexamination proceeding has been granted a filing date and before examiner begins review. Telephone communication is strictly limited to requesting the waiver; merits discussion is not permitted. Agreement/non-agreement is recorded using form PTOL-2292. If waiver is agreed, examiner may issue order and first Office action on the merits on the same day as the order or within a few days thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: General requirement for amendments in reexamination (37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j) and 1.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amendment to the description and claims in patents involved in reexamination proceedings must be made in accordance with § 1.530 and formally presented pursuant to 37 CFR 1.52(a) and (b), and must contain any fees required by 37 CFR 1.20(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must meet formal requirements of 1.52 and the unique provisions of 1.530(d)-(k); excess claim fees per 1.20(c)(3) and (4) may apply where new claims are added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of making specification amendments (37 CFR 1.530(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to the specification, other than to the claims, must be made by submission of the entire text of an added or rewritten paragraph including markings pursuant to paragraph (f) of this section, except that an entire paragraph may be deleted by a statement deleting the paragraph without presentation of the text of the paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The precise point in the specification where the added or rewritten paragraph is located must be identified. All paragraphs added must be submitted as completely underlined. All bracketing and underlining is made in comparison to the original patent (not relative to prior amendments). Blocked paragraphs are assigned letter/number and a caret indicates insertion point — formatting/page layout need not be a concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of making claim amendments (37 CFR 1.530(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment paper must include the entire text of each patent claim being proposed to be changed and of each new claim being proposed to be added. For any claim changed, a parenthetical expression (e.g., “amended”) should follow the claim number. Each changed or added claim must include markings (underlining/brackets) pursuant to paragraph (f); a canceled claim may be canceled by a statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed new claims must be underlined throughout. Examiner’s amendments at NIRC also require full text and markings; requirements apply regardless of submission medium (paper or compact disc).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim status and support requirement (37 CFR 1.530(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever there is an amendment to the claims, there must be supplied, on pages separate from pages containing the changes, the status (pending or canceled) as of the date of the amendment of all patent claims and of all added claims, and an explanation of the support in the disclosure of the patent for the changes to the claims made by the amendment paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit claim status will generally result in an informal response to the patent owner prior to final rejection; failure to set forth the support may lead to the amendment not being entered (especially if submitted after final rejection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required markings for amendments (37 CFR 1.530(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes relative to the patent being reexamined which are made to the specification, including the claims, must include the following markings: matter to be omitted must be enclosed in brackets; matter to be added must be underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Markings are made relative to the original patent and are used later to show exact additions/deletions in the reexamination certificate (underlined matter printed in italics; brackets printed as inserted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim numbering preservation (37 CFR 1.530(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claims may not be renumbered. A patent claim retains its number even if it is canceled in the reexamination proceeding, and the numbering of any added claims must follow the number of the highest numbered patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Canceled claims keep their original numbers; added claims numbering begins after the last original patent claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment substantive limits — no enlargement / no new matter / expiration rules (37 CFR 1.530(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent or introduce new matter. No amendment may be proposed for entry in an expired patent; moreover, no amendment other than cancellation of claims will be incorporated into the patent by a certificate issued after expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments do not become effective until the reexamination certificate is issued and published. If a patent expires during reexamination, all amendments to claims and added claims are withdrawn (diagonal line placed across amended/new claims) and reexamination proceeds on the unamended claims. Examiner should cancel rejected/objected claims so certificate issuance does not attempt to incorporate amendments after expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal paper and electronic submission requirements (37 CFR 1.52(a)-(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers to become part of USPTO permanent records must be on specified paper (A4 or 8.5x11 inches), certain margins, written on one side in portrait, legible machine-printed permanent dark ink, sufficient clarity/contrast for reproduction; no holes recommended; electronic submissions must comply with Office’s electronic filing system requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifications (except reexamination) should be 1½ or double spaced, nonscript font (e.g., Arial, Times Roman, preferably 12), single column; claims and abstracts must begin on separate physical sheets/pages. English language requirement or accompanied by accurate translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of amendments and fees (amendment entry procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments which comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j) and are formally presented pursuant to 37 CFR 1.52(a) and (b), and contain all fees required by 37 CFR 1.20(c), will be entered in the reexamination file pursuant to guidelines in MPEP § 2234.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments submitted after final rejection generally will not be entered; informalities trigger use of form paragraphs (e.g., ¶ 22.12, ¶ 22.13) and may set a shortened statutory period to correct informality (ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS, whichever longer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper amendment handling and notice (form paragraph guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proposed amendment does not comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j), a supplemental paper correctly proposing amendments is required; a shortened statutory period for response may be set to correct the informality, and failure to timely correct may lead to termination of prosecution and issuance of reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs ¶ 22.12 and ¶ 22.13 (or appropriate PTOL forms) in orders/first Office actions to advise patent owner of proper manner of making amendments; after final rejection, amendment should not be entered and patent owner informed using advisory Office action (PTOL-467).

rubrics_metrics.name: All changes made vis-à-vis the patent being reexamined (relative amendment basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments to the patent being reexamined must be made relative to the patent specification in effect as of the date of filing the request for reexamination. If there was a prior change to the patent by a concluded post-patent proceeding, the first amendment must be made relative to the patent specification as changed by the prior proceeding; subsequent amendments are made relative to the patent specification in effect as of the date of filing the request for reexamination, not relative to the prior amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In rare instances where a concluded post-patent proceeding changes the patent while reexamination is pending, amendments will be made relative to the revised patent and 37 CFR 1.530(i) is waived to that extent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner denial process — panel review and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner’s position is to deny reexamination, the examiner will prepare for and set up a panel review conference as per MPEP § 2271.01; if the conference confirms the preliminary decision, the decision denying reexamination will be completed and signed by the examiner, with two or more other conferees initialing the action to indicate their presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A transmittal form PTOL-465 with the third party requester’s address will be completed if a copy for mailing is not available; the concluded reexamination file is annotated (e.g., PALM screens printed and annotated “PROCEEDING CONCLUDED”) and scanned into IFW using the miscellaneous letter document code; file given 420 status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s amendments at Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner’s amendments made at the time the NIRC is prepared also require the full text of any paragraph or claim to be changed, with markings; the exception for examiner’s amendment set forth in 37 CFR 1.121(g) does not apply to reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure full-text presentation and markings even for examiner’s amendments; all bracketing/underlining comparisons are to the original patent.
